q: Which channel sizes break out most, and are their audiences happy? Give n.
a:
Small channels break out most: 36% of the 89 small-channel videos with a baseline were outperformers (110 videos total), compared with 22% for mid (n=50 with baseline) and 5.3% for large (n=38). Average relative lift follows the same order: about 8.0x for small, 3.7x for mid, and 1.3x for large.

Audience sentiment is mixed and fairly close across groups. Net sentiment on product-side comments is +0.06 for small (n=2,717 comments), +0.11 for mid (n=2,354), and -0.03 for large (n=1,965). Mid-size audiences are the happiest, with 41.7% positive against 30.8% negative. Large-channel audiences lean slightly negative (38.8% negative vs 36.2% positive).

Caveat: these are associations from a comment sample, and the large and mid groups have fairly few videos with a baseline, so the outperformer rates are less stable than the comment counts suggest.
sql: WITH v AS (SELECT c.video_id, CASE WHEN cr.tier IN ('nano <50k','micro 50-250k') THEN 'small' WHEN cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' THEN 'mid' WHEN cr.tier IN ('macro 1-5M','mega 5M+') THEN 'large' END AS size_group, p.outperformer, p.rel_lift FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official'), perf AS (SELECT size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, COUNT(outperformer) AS n_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift FROM v GROUP BY size_group), sent AS (SELECT v.size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_raw FROM comments m JOIN v ON v.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY v.size_group) SELECT perf.size_group, perf.n_videos, perf.n_with_baseline, perf.outperformer_rate, perf.avg_rel_lift, sent.n_product_side, sent.pct_positive, sent.pct_negative, CASE WHEN sent.n_product_side>=10 THEN sent.net_raw END AS net_sentiment FROM perf LEFT JOIN sent ON sent.size_group=perf.size_group ORDER BY perf.outperformer_rate DESC LIMIT 40

q: Which content formats work best for mid-sized channels?
a:
First impressions is the only format with a usable sample: 8 of 19 videos (42%, 16 channels) outperformed, with an average relative lift of 2.7. Full review and durability test both show a 100% outperformer rate, but each is a single video (n=1), so that's an anecdote, not a pattern.

Explainer/tips is mixed (n=8): only 12.5% outperformed, yet its average relative lift is high at 9.7, which suggests one or two big hits are pulling the average up. Comparison (n=6), upgrade advice (n=8), meme shorts (n=3), keynote recaps (n=2) and other (n=2) had no outperformers.

Caveat: these are associations in a small mid-tier sample, not proof that a format causes the lift, and most formats have too few videos to rank confidently.
sql: SELECT c.format, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, COUNT(DISTINCT c.channel_id) AS n_channels, ROUND(AVG(p.outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(p.rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift, ROUND(AVG(p.lift),3) AS avg_lift FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' AND p.outperformer IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.format ORDER BY outperformer_rate DESC, avg_rel_lift DESC LIMIT 40

q: Which high-lift videos have the most negative audience reaction? Name two examples, with lift and sentiment shown separately.
a:
Two clear examples: "iPhone Duo's Camera Disappears #shorts" (Time Travel Visuals) and "iPhone FOLD Hands-On | Apple COOKED!" (TechDroider).

The Camera Disappears short has the most negative reaction: net sentiment -0.60 (70% negative, 10% positive, n=77 product-side comments). Its lift is huge, at 499x with 20.5M views (rel_lift 72.9).

The TechDroider hands-on is next: net sentiment -0.52 (70% negative, 18% positive, n=56), with 87x lift on 1.97M views (rel_lift 12.7).

Both have reasonable comment counts, so the sentiment reads are fairly solid. Third place is a Digit Hindi comparison at -0.46, but with only n=24.

Caveat: these are comment samples and show association only. High lift and negative sentiment appearing together doesn't mean the negativity drove the views.
sql: WITH s AS (SELECT video_id, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, AVG(sentiment='positive') AS pos, AVG(sentiment='negative') AS neg FROM comments WHERE lang='en' AND trivial=0 AND target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY video_id HAVING COUNT(*)>=10) SELECT c.video_id, c.title, cr.name AS channel, cr.tier, c.format, p.views, ROUND(p.lift,3) AS lift, ROUND(p.rel_lift,3) AS rel_lift, s.n_product_side, ROUND(s.pos,3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(s.neg,3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(s.pos-s.neg,3) AS net_sentiment FROM content c JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN s ON s.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND p.outperformer=1 ORDER BY net_sentiment ASC, s.n_product_side DESC LIMIT 10

q: Which audience topics are largest, and which are growing fastest this week?
a:
Samsung Did It First is the largest topic (n=822, 8.2% of comments), followed by Eager to Buy (n=571, 5.7%), Praise for review quality (n=543, 5.4%) and Price Complaints (n=479, 4.8%).

The fastest riser is Left-Handed Concerns. It went from 13 comments (1.4% share) to 89 (3.3%), a gain of 2.0 points. Waiting for Next Year is next, from 10 to 51 comments (1.0% to 1.9%). Apple Software Integration (8 to 35) and the reviewer speaking-style criticism topic (4 to 22) also grew, but from small bases. No Face ID grew the most in relative terms (1 to 14), but that n is too small to read much into.

Total comments rose from 954 to 2,666, so most topics grew in raw count. Share change is the better guide. Samsung Did It First lost a little share (-0.7 points) despite its raw growth.

These figures come from a comment sample, so they show associations, not causes.
sql: WITH base AS (SELECT c.topic_id, c.day_since_launch AS d FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id WHERE v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0), mx AS (SELECT MAX(d) AS m FROM base), tot AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS t_all, SUM(d>m-7) AS t_this, SUM(d<=m-7 AND d>m-14) AS t_prev FROM base, mx), agg AS (SELECT topic_id, COUNT(*) AS n_total, SUM(d>m-7) AS n_this, SUM(d<=m-7 AND d>m-14) AS n_prev FROM base, mx WHERE topic_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY topic_id) SELECT t.topic_id, t.name, t.pool, t.origin, t.first_seen, a.n_total, ROUND(1.0*a.n_total/tot.t_all,3) AS share_all, a.n_this, a.n_prev, ROUND(1.0*a.n_this/NULLIF(tot.t_this,0),3) AS share_this_week, ROUND(1.0*a.n_prev/NULLIF(tot.t_prev,0),3) AS share_prev_week, ROUND(1.0*a.n_this/NULLIF(tot.t_this,0)-1.0*a.n_prev/NULLIF(tot.t_prev,0),3) AS share_change, ROUND(1.0*(a.n_this-a.n_prev)/NULLIF(a.n_prev,0),3) AS count_growth, tot.t_this AS all_this_week, tot.t_prev AS all_prev_week FROM agg a JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=a.topic_id, tot ORDER BY a.n_total DESC LIMIT 40

q: How does audience sentiment on the iPhone Duo compare with the iPhone 18 Pro?
a:
The iPhone 18 Pro gets somewhat better net sentiment than the Duo, though the two are close on positivity. Across all product-side comments, the 18 Pro nets +0.122 (n=3,452, 112 videos) versus +0.053 for the Duo (n=7,036, 190 videos). Positive share is nearly identical (39.1% vs 39.3%), but the Duo draws more negativity (33.9% vs 26.9%).

By target:
- Product itself: 18 Pro +0.191 (n=2,814) vs Duo +0.142 (n=4,909).
- Competitor comments: 18 Pro +0.433 (n=231) vs Duo +0.337 (n=826).
- Apple brand: both negative, the 18 Pro far more so (-0.647, n=156) than the Duo (-0.326, n=567).
- Price/value: both negative, with the Duo worse (-0.565, n=734) than the 18 Pro (-0.462, n=251).

Caveat: the 18 Pro's per-target samples are small (n=156 to 251), so those gaps are less reliable. This reflects a comment sample, not causes.
sql: WITH base AS (SELECT c.topic, m.target, m.sentiment, m.video_id FROM comments m JOIN content c ON c.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') AND c.format!='official' AND c.topic IN ('duo','iphone_18_pro')), allrows AS (SELECT topic, 'all product-side' AS target, sentiment, video_id FROM base UNION ALL SELECT topic, target, sentiment, video_id FROM base) SELECT topic, target, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, COUNT(DISTINCT video_id) AS n_videos, ROUND(AVG(sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(sentiment='neutral'),3) AS pct_neutral, ROUND(AVG(sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, CASE WHEN COUNT(*)>=10 THEN ROUND(AVG(sentiment='positive')-AVG(sentiment='negative'),3) END AS net_sentiment FROM allrows GROUP BY topic, target ORDER BY target, topic LIMIT 40

q: What do people like most about the Duo, and what do they criticise most?
a:
The clearest positive is purchase excitement. "Eager to Buy" had 256 positive vs 127 negative comments (n=571), with people wanting to pre-order or upgrade. The Samsung Fold comparison topic (n=448) is 47% positive, but its description suggests many of those commenters are praising Samsung, so I wouldn't read it as love for the Duo. The crease and fold animation is also fairly positive, though split (123 positive, 109 negative, n=271).

The biggest criticisms are price (197 negative, n=479, about 41%), durability doubts about folding phones (179 negative, n=455), and the claim that Apple copied Samsung or came late (324 negative, n=822, but 322 positive, so it's split). The under-display camera skews most negative (125 negative vs 72 positive, n=301).

Caveat: topics overlap and sentiment is often mixed, so treat these as associations in a comment sample.
sql: WITH c AS (SELECT cm.topic_id, cm.sentiment FROM comments cm JOIN content ct ON ct.video_id=cm.video_id WHERE ct.topic='duo' AND ct.format!='official' AND cm.lang='en' AND cm.trivial=0 AND cm.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') AND cm.topic_id IS NOT NULL), agg AS (SELECT t.topic_id, t.name, t.summary, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, SUM(c.sentiment='positive') AS n_pos, SUM(c.sentiment='negative') AS n_neg, ROUND(1.0*SUM(c.sentiment='positive')/COUNT(*),3) AS pos_share, ROUND(1.0*SUM(c.sentiment='negative')/COUNT(*),3) AS neg_share FROM c JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=c.topic_id GROUP BY t.topic_id) SELECT * FROM (SELECT 'liked' AS side, name, summary, n_product_side, n_pos, n_neg, pos_share, neg_share FROM agg ORDER BY n_pos DESC LIMIT 8) UNION ALL SELECT * FROM (SELECT 'criticised' AS side, name, summary, n_product_side, n_pos, n_neg, pos_share, neg_share FROM agg ORDER BY n_neg DESC LIMIT 8)
